entries.summary: Host adapters can compute the instruction frozen by K8 sync with botTurnInstruction on the host-kit entry, using an options object and InstructionLimits.

Store lease and gate release failures preserve a refused ServiceInstallationError and its code, with the refusal and all release failures in its AggregateError cause; Hosts that matched the 0.42.0 AggregateError on first install must read cause instead. The code follows the outcome (#2010): a call that leaves its receipt pending or its stores unrestored throws upgrade_pending with every failure in its cause, so the Host runs recover(), first restarting the Host process if a stuck lease makes it fail with store_busy; a preparation error that is not the SDK's own is the new store_preparation_failed with the original error as its cause. The same type gains install_root_foreign_owner (#2001): every ServiceInstallation operation holds an install-root gate, so a second operation on one install root fails at once with lifecycle_owner_busy, and an install root owned by another user is refused before anything changes. The receipt commit protocol (#2011) adds receipt_upgrade_required, receipt_state_inconsistent, switch_unhealthy, repair_interrupted and service_program_not_current (see service-upgrade-receipt-v2), and store_overlaps_service_state: a precheck store or a snapshot entry that is, holds or lies in a daemon store's service/ directory is refused before it is snapshotted or restored.

upgrade-receipt.json is version 2 (#2011): ServiceUpgradeReceipt.version is 2 and a pending receipt carries kind (upgrade, rollback or repair). recover() acts on the kind, the code and where current points, starting a present current as it is instead of restoring the snapshot over its writes; a candidate found unhealthy is failed with switch_unhealthy and nothing starts, and an interrupted same-version reinstall is repair_interrupted. A pending version 1 receipt is receipt_upgrade_required: run recover() with SDK 0.42 before upgrading the SDK; a final one reads as version 2 and the next write stores version 2. Hosts that parse the receipt accept version 2 and kind; Hosts that switch on codes handle the five new ServiceInstallationErrorCode values. createServiceInstallation refuses a program that does not run from current, and upgrade() and rollback() a unit the SDK did not write, with service_program_not_current.

macOS Keychain and Linux Secret Service report an SDK entry that does not decode as the new KEYCHAIN_SECRET_CORRUPTED instead of KEYCHAIN_SECRET_DECODE_FAILED, and ProviderRegistry.replaceSecret/configure overwrite it with a new key. KEYCHAIN_SECRET_DECODE_FAILED now means an entry the SDK did not write; the registry never overwrites it and refuses before any write. A Host that offered 'enter the key again' for KEYCHAIN_SECRET_DECODE_FAILED offers it for KEYCHAIN_SECRET_CORRUPTED and shows delete, rename or other-profile guidance for KEYCHAIN_SECRET_DECODE_FAILED.

cancelHostIntents atomically cancels selected unsubmitted Host intents without a pass. HostIntentError.rejected lists all refused keys and code gains inflight; update exhaustive switches. Existing cancelHostIntent, drainForSwitch and abortSwitch behavior and store format are unchanged. Hosts may replace freeze, individual cancels and abort with this call, retaining freeze when other device work must be held. Successors wait for a later pass or an explicit drain().

The local bot-collaboration entry exports inspectLedger(path, tenant), a read-only precheck returning StoreCompatibility. It reports migration-required for would-do rows without turnId; run migrateWouldDo after snapshot and before serving. LocalStoreId gains bot-collaboration-ledger; Hosts with exhaustive switches or Record<LocalStoreId, ...> must add this member.

Custom LocalTaskJournal implementations must accept the new cutoff argument of pruneConfirmedJournalTask(taskId, cutoff) (#1990) and recheck it in the delete transaction under the write lock. It returns false and deletes nothing when the task is valid but not prunable: a confirmed terminal last updated at or after cutoff, or a received offer whose first stored task.cancel sequenced above the offer was committed at or after cutoff (including evidence replaced under the same task id) or that has no such cancellation. For a received offer it throws and deletes nothing when the task.cancel that qualifies it fails its hash or enrollment check, names another task id, or carries a seq different from its row's. A confirmed terminal's envelopes, withheld rows and the task's other envelopes are not verified before deletion. An implementation that ignores cutoff still compiles but can delete unexpired or replaced evidence; the SDK does not repeat these checks.

A path mutation gate release that fails while another error is thrown is kept: PathMutationGateBusyError, ServiceUnitError and LocalStateRelocation errors keep their class and code with an AggregateError of the original error and the release failures in cause, and an error of another class from a managed service lifecycle operation becomes that AggregateError. ServiceUnitError and the LocalStateRelocation error classes accept ErrorOptions. Hosts that read the original error of such a failure read it from cause.

clearDeviceEnrollment and Daemon.unpair() no longer delete another store's credential or staged first pairing under the same productId: they hold a per-user productId lock from validation through deletion, and pairing takes it across its credential writes, each waiting up to 30 seconds. FirstPairingAttempt gains storeIdentity (DeviceStore.identity, the SHA-256 hex of the resolved storeDir); an injected DeviceCredentialBackend keeps every attempt field, or the store's own attempt is refused. A clear refuses another store's attempt as store_not_bound and an attempt that names no store (staged by 0.42.0) with the new DeviceEnrollmentClearErrorCode pairing_attempt_unattributed; clearDeviceEnrollment({ ..., clearUnattributedAttempt: true }) deletes it. Pairing applies the same rule (#2033): it reuses only its own store's staged attempt and otherwise throws the new FirstPairingAttemptRefusedError (store_not_bound, which replaceOtherStore discards, or pairing_attempt_unattributed). A running daemon's token renewal takes the same lock around its write and writes only while the OS entry still holds its store's enrollment; otherwise the daemon halts as store_not_bound or re_pair_required (#2034). A renewal never holds the lock across a network request. A pairing is one critical section: it rereads the enrollment and staged attempt under the lock, never a cached record, refuses another store's or an unattributed attempt even beside its own enrollment, and holds the lock across its own request, because server registration has no fencing, and through its E2EE member entries. BlobClient and InstallSkillPacksOptions change only through the types they reference (#1964).
